sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (sha256 6d44970b...; read in memory with openpyxl read_only): 'Quality Checks' row 3 (#2 instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice: 'Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.') and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 3 (identical text; no extra annotation column populated for this row)
evidence: Skill procedure (quality-checks.md:14-15): verify sentence variety, contractions, occasional terse fragment; defects are uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, or voice change between instruction.md and notes. instruction.md is first-person, conversational and varied: opens with a question (line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?'), uses colloquial phrasing ('nobody's work gets trampled' line 1; 'is ours to arrange' line 3; 'tell me who' line 3; 'I often move several candidates together' line 3; 'layout and names are yours' line 11; 'is your call' line 13; 'if that helps' line 13), contractions (don't x2, it's, mustn't, nobody's), and mixes short and long sentences ('We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' line 11). No bullets or headings in the brief. A grep over instruction.md and both notes for marketing/LLM gloss (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, ensure, intuitive, comprehensive, streamline, elevate) found no hits. Line 13 is a dense runtime-contract sentence but phrased the way a developer would hand off a contract ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call'), not a spec-sheet list. hireops_rules.md keeps the same team voice ('our recruiting workspace', 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' lines 3-5; 'between our side and the candidate' line 127; 'Where drafts are kept is yours' line 175); its tables/bullets are natural for a rules note and are not perfectly parallel boilerplate (e.g. line 49-51 rejection bullets differ in structure). Observations considered and judged non-defects: (a) hireops_rules.md section 8 'Runtime file paths' (lines 196-202) shifts to an impersonal ops register ('The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory...') - plausible as a platform engineer's note, bounded to one short section; (b) spelling mix 'honour'/'honouring' (instruction.md:13) vs 'Honor' (hireops_rules.md:201) vs 'honoring' (integration.md:7, template-controlled text) - a small human inconsistency, not robotic prose; (c) uneven hard wraps at hireops_rules.md lines 91-92, 99, 112, 173 indicate hand edits rather than generated text and do not affect reading. Plausible failing alternative considered: a brief in uniform bullet form with 'seamless, robust collaboration' gloss would fail; this brief does not. A conforming alternative (terser casual brief) would also pass, so the row does not demand polish. This is a text-only judgement row; no runtime evidence is required, so no measurement gap applies to it.
